Treaties are interpreted under Articles 31–33 of the Vienna Convention on the Law of Treaties, which reflect customary international law. A treaty is read in good faith according to the ordinary meaning of its terms in their context and in light of its object and purpose, together with any subsequent agreement or practice of the parties and other relevant rules of international law. Preparatory work and the circumstances of conclusion are supplementary means, used to confirm that reading or when the meaning is ambiguous, obscure, or manifestly absurd or unreasonable.
CONFIDENCE: 92
